mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same quarter indicates weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10% in same quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of triggered quarters, or the average return exceeds the market median by one standard deviation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during periods of sustained low unemployment at 10% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate by more than 0.75 percentage points signals an emergency monetary easing, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during episodes of such emergency rate cuts, or the median return is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise of more than 1% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) within the same month signals a synchronized expansion in demand components, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both show monthly change > 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered months, or the average return is below the market median.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) increase of more than 100,000 alongside an unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months signals a labor market that is expanding but still slack, which supports earnings growth without excessive wage inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 100000 AND UNRATE > 5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 50% of triggered periods, or the mean return is below the long-run market average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.6% for six consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which increases corporate revenues and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.6% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 70% of triggered periods, or the median return is below the 25th percentile of historical returns.
